listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Wednesday, November 11. Our lead story is from Congo. The government said today that its Ebola outbreak has passed 11,000 cases. It is the deadliest outbreak the country has seen. Officials describe a relentless spread of the disease. The figure shows how severe the situation has become. More detail on the response is not yet available. Now the front page. In Washington, House Republicans used a procedural move to short-circuit a floor vote on the impeachment effort against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The effort was brought by Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie. It has effectively ended for now. In tech, Google's Gemini 4 Carbon is now available to everyone. It was first limited to a subset of cyber defenders. It is priced at two dollars per million input tokens and ten dollars per million output tokens. In baseball, Braves general manager Alex Anthopoulos shut down talk of trading Ronald Acuna Junior. He said he has no idea where that came from, and that the team needs him. In Spain, workers are on strike today for the first general strike in fourteen years. They want action on the housing crisis, less than three weeks before a national election. Now the sections. In tech and AI, Anthropic has launched a roadshow for its proposed initial public offering. It is also committing a portion of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund. And the Claude quickstarts repository offers starter projects for building with the Claude API. In politics, a federal appeals court says forcing companies to disclose major sources of climate pollution is likely unconstitutional. Drop Site News reports the U.S. is sending military assets to the Middle East as talks falter. And House Republicans elected Jim Jordan as their leader. In world news, Russia and Ukraine held nearly four hours of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi. Separately, a U.S. general warns about Madagascar's growing military ties with Russia. In sports, the 49ers traded for receiver Keenan Allen and placed lineman Gracen Halton on injured reserve. The Rockets, eight and three, host a Warriors team seeking its ninth straight win. In Atlanta, a vacant strip of Old Fourth Ward near the Beltline is on the market. A 382-unit project is coming into view along Georgia 400 in Sandy Springs. And the Pendergrast Farm pocket neighborhood is now complete. In architecture, SketchUp 2027 improves Revit interoperability. Ageiro launched Ark Watcher to monitor project data across several platforms. And ArchDaily looks at drone imagery in urban analysis. In science, Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth on November 18. Neurotechnology to restore speech is moving fast. And new research says rising seas could reshape habitats for more than forty percent of land vertebrates. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Ebola tops 11,000 cases in Congo's deadliest outbreak
lead.note: Congo's government said on Wednesday that its Ebola outbreak has passed 11,000 cases. The outbreak is described as the deadliest the country has faced. The figure is presented as a stark measure of how serious the situation has become, as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease. The summary does not give further detail on deaths, regions affected or the response, so those questions remain open for now. For a reader following world news, the main point is the scale. An outbreak that has crossed 11,000 cases is far larger than a local flare-up, and the government's own language points to continued spread rather than containment. It is the kind of story worth checking again in coming days, as officials release updated counts and more detail on how the country and its partners are responding.
